Hey Oliver - thanks for the screenshot and for flagging this. Sorry for the friction.

Short answer: Calendly usually detects timezone from the browser, but we've seen cases where the link encodes a fallback timezone (or the browser profile is stuck on a different zone). There’s also a DST mismatch edge-case between US/EU that can show unexpected offsets around mid-March.

Workarounds I can do right away:
- I can manually send a calendar invite for Tue Mar 16 at 16:00 CET (which should show as 11:00 AM ET).
- Or you can try changing the timezone in the Calendly page (dropdown at the top right) or open the link in an incognito window - that usually forces the correct detection.

Would you like me to send an invite directly? If yes I’ll attach an .ics and confirm the time in your timezone.

Great - invite sent (attached: redwood-demo-invite.ics). Just a note for transparency:

- Why this happens: US daylight savings started on Mar 8, 2026, but EU switches later in March. Calendly and browser timezone detection sometimes surface the US offset until the client device/browser is refreshed. If you ever see weird offsets, changing the timezone selector on the Calendly page or using incognito usually fixes it.
- Long-term workaround: we can also white-label a scheduling page that forces the TZ or share specific time slots in an email (what we did here).

Time conversion: Tue Mar 16, 16:00 CET = Tue Mar 16, 11:00 AM ET = Tue Mar 16, 19:00 MSK (if relevant).

Looking forward to the demo. If for any reason the .ics shows a different time on your calendar, reply and I’ll resend with a confirmed UTC timestamp.

Cheers,
